title: add postgres restore bootstrapping, schema-drift preflight and downgrade gate
author: Asha Nair
description:
Motivation: customers running Redwood Private reported two correlated issues during multi-stage upgrades: (1) intermittent restore failures when bringing up an older control plane from a newer DB state, and (2) upgrades that included non-reversible schema migrations accidentally allowing downgrades to proceed. This PR adds a pragmatic, operator-friendly restore bootstrapping flow for Postgres backups, a lightweight schema-drift preflight validator, and a downgrade gate that blocks non-reversible downgrade attempts.

What this change does (high level):
- Adds an idempotent restore bootstrap script (installer/scripts/pg_restore_bootstrap.sh) that performs ordered steps: restore base snapshot -> apply reversible shim migrations -> populate migration_metadata table -> run post-restore consistency checks. The script is safe to re-run and publishes a restore-token to S3 to avoid concurrent restores.
- Introduces a schema-drift preflight check in the installer (installer/preflight/schema_drift_check.go) used by both the Helm pre-upgrade hook and the rwictl CLI. The check compares current DB schema fingerprint against the expected release fingerprint and fails fast if incompatible, with clear operator-facing remediation hints.
- Adds a downgrade gate to the private installer that inspects the release's migration manifest. If the manifest contains migrations marked "non-reversible", the gate prevents applying a release with an older version unless an explicit --force-downgrade WITH operator confirmation is supplied. This is enforced in the Helm pre-upgrade hook and Terraform plan validation.
- Helm: add pre-upgrade and post-restore hooks to perform safe snapshot creation and to run the schema preflight before live traffic is switched (helm/templates/pre-upgrade-snapshot-hook.yaml, helm/templates/post-restore-hook.yaml).
- Terraform: add restore verification resources and data sources (terraform/modules/backup/restore.tf) that can be used in automated restore pipelines to assert restore-token and checksum match.
- CLI: extend rwictl restore workflow with a --bootstrap flag and progress output (installer/cli/rwictl/restore.go).
- Docs: add an operator playbook with step-by-step restore and downgrade guidance (docs/ops/restore-playbook.md).

Why this is different from previous work: prior PRs focused on atomic migration rollbacks and snapshot preservation; this one focuses on making restores idempotent and safe when control plane versions and DB schemas diverge, plus an explicit downgrade safety gate tied to migration metadata.

Testing and validation: unit tests for schema fingerprinting and migration manifest parsing were added (tests/unit/schema_drift_test.go). An e2e roundtrip test was added that runs a restore -> bootstrap -> upgrade -> downgrade cycle (tests/e2e/restore_roundtrip_test.go). During CI we observed a flaky e2e that required an extra retry boundary; the test harness was hardened.

Upgrade notes for operators: follow docs/ops/restore-playbook.md. For automated restores use the terraform data source to verify restore-token before promoting traffic. To bypass the downgrade gate you must run rwictl restore --from-s3 <snapshot> --bootstrap --allow-unsafe-downgrade and acknowledge the risk; this flag is intentionally noisy in logs.

Security notes: restore tokens are short-lived and stored encrypted in S3 with KMS. The bootstrap script enforces least-privilege assumptions (separate restore role) and writes audit entries to the installer audit log.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add bootstrap script and CLI plumbing
- [x] Add Helm hooks and Terraform verify resources
- [x] Add schema-drift preflight and tests
- [x] Update operator docs and playbook
- [x] Run and stabilize e2e restore roundtrip

Rollout plan: ship in v1.8.4 as part of the private-installer patch release. Operators should schedule a backup snapshot before applying the new installer and run a restore dry-run using the terraform verify data source.

review_comments: Samir Patel (2026-02-16): Please add explicit unit tests for the restore-token expiry path — I saw a flake locally when token rotation occurs.
Asha Nair (2026-02-16): Added token expiry unit tests and updated the bootstrap to early-exit on expiry; PTAL.
Evelyn Chen (2026-02-17): The schema fingerprint algorithm needs to tolerate comment-only changes; added suggestion to canonicalize by ignoring COMMENT statements.
Asha Nair (2026-02-17): Implemented canonicalization and added a test vector. Also updated docs to mention comment-only drift is ignored.

Liam O'Connor (2026-02-18): Can we make the Helm pre-upgrade hook idempotent across failed hook runs? Observed helm retry causing double snapshot creation.
Response: converted snapshot creation to a create-if-not-exists flow keyed by release name.
Samir Patel (2026-02-19): e2e started failing on CI due to timing around primary promotion; added a retry with exponential backoff in the test harness. Rerun CI.
release_notes: Operator-facing: add idempotent Postgres restore bootstrap, schema-drift preflight, Helm pre-upgrade snapshot hooks, and a downgrade safety gate. See docs/ops/restore-playbook.md for runbook.
